issues.claim: Partly fixed. Round 6 defined a public note's marker in a picture for a building (Find's pole of inaccessibility), an area, a point thing, and 'any other thing — a plot, a way, a wall — at its anchor point by kind, V10 §3.6 rule 1's `EntityCard.anchor`' (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`, l. 16323–16329). Two cases are still open. (a) Things with no point or shape of their own. V09 §4.19 (l. 2907) lets an owner or editor write a public note on any thing's About tab. The context panel opens for every registry kind (V09 §4.4, l. 1760–1772): a use (its Links tab), an institution, a room, a Works record, a raised way's span or crossing (V09 §4.20.6). V10 §3.6 rule 1 (l. 1561–1565) names only districts, quarters and regions, plots, buildings, ways, wall traces, retaining walls, coasts, river courses, gates, towers, pins, lights, access points and lakes, with no rule for any other kind. So a note on an inn's use, an institution, a person, a room, a record or a span has no marker point. One builder draws it at the use's building, another leaves it out, a third lists it on the legend sheet with no marker. (b) The frame and layers. A picture can be framed on a district, the selection or a rectangle (V09 §5.10, l. 4071), which can leave a view pin or a noted thing outside the frame. A noted thing can also lie on a layer the picture does not draw (a tunnel's note in a ground picture). T-ER-19's outcome 'every pin drawn' (l. 16906) does not say what happens to such a marker or its legend entry. This is an annotated picture, a normal path, with no defined outcome, and T-ER-19 runs only a building, a way and a withheld building.
issues.required_change: Rendering, with VAT-r6-01 (which homes the anchor rule) and an END at V09. (1) §11.2's `ExportOpts.pins` comment: replace 'any other thing — a plot, a way, a wall — at its anchor point by kind, V10 §3.6 rule 1's `EntityCard.anchor`)' with 'any other thing at its `EntityCard.anchor` (§11.2's rule by kind: a use, an institution, a room, a person or a record at the anchor of the thing that holds it))'. After 'numbered from 1,' add 'a pin or a note whose marker point lies outside the picture's frame, or whose thing lies on a layer the picture does not draw, has no marker and no legend entry, the numbers running on without it,'. (2) T-ER-19's input: 'and holding a public note on a building, one on a way and one on a building the export's key withholds' adds ', one on a use, one on a building outside a district-framed picture and one on a tunnel in a ground picture'. Its outcome adds 'the use's marker at its building's `EntityCard.anchor`, numbered in address order with the rest; the out-of-frame and other-layer notes with no marker and no legend entry'. (3) END at V09's entity table, notes row (l. 4171): 'each public note a numbered marker at its thing' adds ' (at its `EntityCard.anchor`, §11.2, where its thing has no point or shape of its own; none for a thing outside the picture's frame or layers)'.

issues.claim: The matrix misses `EntityCard.anchor`'s per-kind rule, a subject shared by rendering (§11.2), V09 and V10. `anchor: PointCm` is a required field of §11.2's `EntityCard` (l. 16488). Its type is §11.2's (R2-10), and the base's facade fills it for every registry kind from M3a (`query entity`, file f item 468). The base states no rule for it. The only rule is V10 §3.6 rule 1 (l. 1561–1565), the clerk resolver's `{ at: r }`. Three places cite that rule as the field's definition: V09 l. 2643 ('a named target's point is always the target's `EntityCard.anchor` (V10 §3.6 rule 1)', with T101-3's byte parity between canvas and clerk), V10's resolver ('reads positions from the reader's `EntityCard`', l. 1558), and since round 6 §11.2's own `ExportOpts.pins`. So the base producer's rule sits in a later volume, and it is incomplete. It gives no anchor for a use, an institution, a household, a person, a room, a storey or tier, a record (a Works, a mutation plan, a condition overlay), a raised way's span or crossing, a tunnel, an island, a field, a green, a square or a camp. Yet every card carries a required `anchor`, and V10 §3.6 rule 10 resolves `{ anchor }` by rules 1–7 with no fallback. Two builders of the facade would build different points: a district's centroid against V10's label-spine midpoint, and any point at all for a use. V09's named-target point, the clerk's resolved point and a public note's marker then disagree with V09's and V10's text.
issues.required_change: Rendering, with ENDs at V10 and V09. (1) §11.2's `EntityCard`: `anchor: PointCm;` takes the comment: '/* the entity's anchor point by kind, one rule, read by V10 §3.6's resolver, V09's named targets and ExportOpts.pins: a district, neighbourhood, quarter or region — the midpoint of its first area-label spine (S13a's candidate, §9.3); a plot, a building or any other face (a field, a green, a square, a camp, an island's key) — its centroid, or the largest inscribed rectangle's centre (§3.4's `lir`) where the centroid falls outside it; a lake — its polygon's inscribed centre; a way, a wall trace, a retaining wall, a coast, a river course or a tunnel — the point at half its length from its first end; a raised way's span — the point at half its length, a crossing — its point; a gate, tower, pin, light, access point or any other point thing — its point; a thing with no geometry of its own — a use, an institution or a household at the anchor of its first building in address order (with none, of its plot), a person at their household's, a room, a storey or a tier at its building's, a record (a Works, a mutation plan, a condition overlay) at its first target's in address order; with none of these, the growth centre (S3's root reservation, §4.2) */'. (2) END at V10 §3.6 rule 1: 'the entity's anchor point, by kind: a district, quarter or region — … a lake — its polygon's inscribed centre.' → 'the entity's anchor point, §11.2's `EntityCard.anchor` (its rule by kind).' (3) END at V09 l. 2643: '(V10 §3.6 rule 1)' → '(§11.2's rule by kind)'. (4) END at V10's T-V10-8: the `entity` goldens add one entity of each kind the rule names, its `anchor` by the rule.

issues.claim: A gate's grip slid into a raised way's under-deck strip has two outcomes. V09 §4.9's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` (l. 2103) gives a gate form 'for a gate dropped or slid inside the under-deck strip (T3's **Gate**, a gate's grip)': 'No gate can stand beneath {way}, so it moves {m} m along {wall}.' So a slid gate goes back along the wall and the trace is unchanged. A gate's grip is `moveVertex` on the gate's crossing vertex, 'the crossing way follows' (V09 l. 1194, l. 1703; §7.1 l. 10733: '`moveVertex` on an enceinte's trace — … a gate's crossing among them'). That makes it 'a moved trace vertex', which is row W2 of §2.7's crossing table. W2·C2 reads 'through a gate moved clear of the strip', and its last column says 'a gate it makes for a ground way inside the under-deck strip moved along that way clear of it, the stretch bent locally through it'. §7.1's row (l. 10674) says the same. So in the base the gate moves along its way and the trace bends off its line round the deck strip to pass through it. Only W13 (a `placeGate`) moves a gate along the trace. *beneath*'s gate clause (l. 2646–2652) offers both forms, the second 'where the way is laid after the gate and follows it'. No cell names the slid gate, and no test runs it: T110-2 (4) (l. 18581) and T-V9-52 run only a dropped gate. A builder of the base bends the wall; a builder of V09's line expects it to stay on its line. That is two units with two outcomes for one case, and an untested edge.
issues.required_change: Model (§2.7's crossing table), with ENDs at determinism, scope and V09. (1) §2.7's row W13: '**W13** a hand `placeGate` (§7.1's sugar: a stub crossing the trace at `at`)' → '**W13** a hand `placeGate` (§7.1's sugar: a stub crossing the trace at `at`), or a gate's crossing vertex slid along the trace by `moveVertex` (V09's gate grip)'. Its C2 cell: 'at an `at` inside the under-deck strip, bent along the trace to the nearest point clear of it, the stub with it' → 'at an `at` or a slid point inside the under-deck strip, bent along the trace to the nearest point clear of it, the stub or the crossing way following it, the trace unchanged'. Row W2's event cell: 'a hand `drawWall`, a moved trace vertex or a re-anchored stretch' adds '(a gate's slid crossing vertex is W13)'. (2) END at determinism §7.1's row (l. 10674): 'or a `placeGate` inside its under-deck strip' → 'or a `placeGate` or a gate's slid crossing vertex (`moveVertex`) inside its under-deck strip'. Also 'a `placeGate` moved along the trace clear of the under-deck strip' → 'a `placeGate` or a slid gate moved along the trace clear of the under-deck strip, its way following'. (3) END at scope's T110-2 (4): after 'a hand `placeGate` inside a viaduct's under-deck strip — moved along the trace clear of it, `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`;' add 'a gate's grip slid along the trace into that strip — moved back along the trace clear of it, its way following, the trace unchanged, `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s gate form;'. (4) END at V09's T-V9-52: after 'a gate dropped on that wall inside the viaduct's under-deck strip moves along the trace clear of it, with `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s gate form' add ', and a gate's grip slid into that strip moves back along the trace clear of it, the trace unchanged, with the same line'.

issues.claim: Two words at V01 left behind by R6-10's END. (a) V01 §5.1.3 (l. 3037–3039) now reads 'the hood pins, model pins and access symbols belong to the `pins` group and block trees to the `trees` group, so the view bar hides them as Neighbourhood's keys do'. The switches are the Dress panel's (T12 `dress`: V09 l. 1825, l. 4003; §8.4 l. 13677). V09's view bar (l. 3799) holds the layer toggles (§7.8) and no group switch, and 'Neighbourhood's keys' names nothing in the set. (b) §3.18 (c)'s row (l. 2624) gives the group switches the outcome 'view only'. The same table's Find row uses 'view only' to mean the log is byte-identical, yet each switch is a logged `setStyle` (§8.2 l. 12601; T-V1-56 (c): 'logged as one `setStyle`'). A builder follows §8.2 and T-V1-56, so nothing built changes.

(2) §3.18 (c): split the row '| the `pins` and `trees` group switches (`StyleSheet.groups`); the style's `details` and `shadows` | view only (V01 §5.1.2, V01 §5.1.3) |' into '| the `pins` and `trees` group switches (`StyleSheet.groups`) | style only: one logged `setStyle` each, undone as a style edit, the model digest unchanged (§7.4's style row; V01 §5.1.3) |' and '| the style's `details` and `shadows` | view only (V01 §5.1.2, V01 §5.1.3) |'.

issues.claim: `bend.raised.underSpan`'s line does not fit the case round 6 added. §7.1's row (l. 10675) and §2.7's way-and-channel table row (b)'s gates cell now send a hand way 'crossing an enceinte's trace inside that strip' to `bend.raised.underSpan`, its crossing of the trace 'moved along the deck to the nearest crossing clear of the strip'. V09 §4.9's row (l. 2104) copies that source cell, but its one line, '{name} passes under {way} through its nearest open arch, {m} m off your line.', words only the arch case. The key, its event and the bend are the same, so nothing built changes; the sentence is wrong for the case (T-V9-52's 'a road drawn across that wall there crosses it clear of the strip, with `bend.raised.underSpan`').

issues.claim: The shared subject `StyleSheet.groups` stops at the canvas and never reaches the clerk's tool. R6-10 made the trees and pins drawing groups style state, switched by a logged `setStyle` of `StyleSheet.groups`, 'and no drawing group by `setLayer`' (§8.4 l. 13677–13678; §2.1 l. 555–556; §8.2 l. 12601). V09's T12 `dress` gained the **Trees** and **Pins** switches (l. 1825: 'Trees and Pins → `setStyle` of `StyleSheet.groups`'). V10's T12 tool did not follow. `DressInput` (l. 935) has `layer?: { layer: string; visible: boolean }`, encoded as `setLayer { layer, spec: { visible } }` (V10 §4.1's T12 row, l. 2821), and no member for a group. The tool description (l. 1425) offers 'layer visibility'. So 'hide the trees' asked of the clerk has no encoder form. One builder passes `layer: 'trees'` into a `setLayer` whose `Layer` (§2.1: underground, ground, sky) does not admit it, and the request fails where V09's switch succeeds. Another reaches for the escape hatch with a guessed row operation. Canvas and clerk then write different bytes for one declaration (T101-3). T-V10-4, which runs 'every tool and every input form', has no such form to run. R6-10's sweep reached V01, V04, V09, model and pipeline, but not V10's `dress`.
issues.required_change: V10. (1) `DressInput`: 'layer?: { layer: string; visible: boolean }' → 'layer?: { layer: Layer /* §2.1: underground, ground or sky; a drawing group's name fails the schema, an is_error result with no event (V10 §3.4 (3)) */; visible: boolean }; groups?: { trees?: boolean; pins?: boolean } /* T12's Trees and Pins switches: §8.2's StyleSheet.groups — trees every tree instance and block tree, pins every model pin, hood pin and ground-access symbol */'. (2) §4.1's T12 `dress` row: the inputs cell '`preset`, `layer`, `restyle`' → '`preset`, `layer`, `groups`, `restyle`'. The events cell adds '; `groups` → the `setStyle` of `StyleSheet.groups` that V09's Trees and Pins switches emit, one row operation per member given (§8.2; V09 §4.5's T12 row), the bytes of those switches'. (3) The `dress` tool description (l. 1425): 'and layer visibility' → ', layer visibility and the trees and pins switches'. (4) T-V10-4 adds: '`dress { groups: { trees: false } }` and V09's Trees switch give one `setStyle`, byte for byte; `dress { layer: { layer: 'trees', visible: false } }` gives an is_error result with no event'.

issues.claim: One word, 'Pins', now names two concepts on V09's screens (principle (2)). The Dress panel's new switch for §8.2's `StyleSheet.groups.pins` — model pins, hood pins and ground-access symbols — is labelled **Pins** (l. 1742, l. 1825, l. 4003). §4.19's **Pins** control (l. 2908: 'Add a pin', view pins) and the Picture tab's **pins and public notes** (l. 4071; §11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`) mean the view pins. A user who turns the Dress panel's Pins off sees every view pin still drawn. Nothing built changes; the label names the wrong concept.
